name: Sarson Ka Saag
description: Punjabi sarson ka saag with mustard greens and spinach slowly cooked with ginger, garlic and chillies, then thickened lightly with maize flour and finished with ghee tempering.
ingredients: 750 g mustard greens (sarson), cleaned and chopped
method: Wash the mustard greens and spinach thoroughly in several changes of water to remove grit, drain and chop roughly.
Add the greens to a large pot with the green chillies, ginger, part of the garlic, salt and only a small splash of water. Cover and cook gently until very soft.
Mash the cooked greens for a rustic texture, or pulse briefly with a blender if you prefer them finer; avoid turning the saag completely smooth unless that is your preferred style.
Stir in the maize flour gradually so it does not form dry lumps, then simmer on low heat until the saag thickens and the raw flour taste disappears.
For the tempering, heat the ghee and cook the chopped onion with the remaining garlic until golden and aromatic.
Pour the hot tempering over the saag, stir through or leave partly visible on top, taste for salt and serve hot with makki di roti.
